nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.

This imposes unsupported constraints and can lose the rubric’s progress/endpoint meaning.
audit.source_clause: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment.
audit.counterexample: If the requested DVD is visibly white but its DVD identity cannot be established, the program cannot return complete because it requires both whiteness and DVD identity. If matching evidence is unknown while other evidence establishes that the original target remains black, the required match can also prevent the program from returning absent. The original rubric does not add an identity-preservation condition or require every evidence path to be resolved when the outcome is otherwise established.

The repeated passes and reference disagreement do not establish a visual answer; the rejected construction and audit failures are not visual evidence.

program.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court
requirements.source_phrase: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show a basketball court as the background, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the background is visibly a basketball court with recognizable court features. Fail if the background is clearly not a basketball court. Unknown if the background or its features cannot be assessed reliably.
nodes.binding: The requested outcome is to replace the image background with a basketball court; judge the edited image against that outcome.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has begun changing toward a basketball court, even though the requested court background is not complete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows a discernible but incomplete change of the background toward a basketball court. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that change. Unknown if progress cannot be distinguished from the original or assessed reliably.
nodes.binding: Assess progress only toward replacing the background with a basketball court; unrelated edits do not count.

nodes.question: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
nodes.criteria: Return yes if support 1 passes: the requested basketball-court background is complete. Otherwise, return no only if support 1 fails and support 2 fails, establishing no requested progress. Return partial if support 1 fails and support 2 passes, establishing incomplete requested progress. Return unknown if the evidence needed to distinguish these alternatives is unresolved. A skipped support is unobserved, not a failure: if support 1 is skipped, support 2 passing establishes partial progress, but support 2 failing alone cannot establish no progress or completion, so return unknown. Supporting evidence earns no completion credit independently; unrelated edits do not count.

program.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
nodes.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

nodes.question: Does comparison with the input image show that the requested chalk-drawing transformation has progressed?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comparison shows some change toward rendering the image as a chalk drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete. Fail if there is no requested progress; unrelated edits alone do not count. Unknown if the images or comparison are insufficient to determine progress.
nodes.binding: O1 and the rubric: assess progress toward the requested chalk-drawing transformation, not unrelated edits.

nodes.question: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1. Return yes only when support 1 passes: the edited image is a chalk-made drawing. Return no only when support 1 fails and support 2 fails, establishing no requested progress. Return partial when support 1 fails and support 2 passes, establishing some but incomplete requested progress. Return unknown when the evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved. Support 2 is conditionally skipped when support 1 passes; that skipped observation remains unobserved, and the endpoint evidence alone establishes completion. A skipped support does not count as a failure or as evidence of progress. Unrelated edits never count as requested progress.
